reply.thought: The handoff claims the refunds are applied, but I must verify against the refunds table myself before paying anyone. Starting with list_refunds.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly: orders 150, 151, and 155 with the same amounts. I can now check the orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly for orders 150, 151, and 155. The orders map to customers acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 9958 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance so I can pay each customer.
Acme and birch net balances are in hand, and the refunds table matched the batch. Cobalt's net balance is the last one I need before recording payouts.

The refunds table matches the batch exactly for orders 150, 151, and 155, and I have all three net balances. Each customer gets one payout equal to their net_balance figure, so I'll start by recording acme's payout of 9958 cents.
Acme's payout of 9958 cents recorded successfully. Birch's net balance is 42141 cents, and that matches orders 151 and 154 less the 15870 refund, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch payouts are recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 50848 matches orders 152 and 155 (36736 + 18321) less the 4209 refund on order 155, so I'll record that payout now.

All three payouts are recorded. I checked the arithmetic: acme 18740+3900-12682=9958, birch 25496+32515-15870=42141, and cobalt 36736+18321-4209=50848. Each matches its net_balance result, and the refunds table matched the batch exactly before any payout.
